articles.title: CISA Warns SafePay Ransomware Has Hit 600+ Organizations and Destroyed Backup Systems
articles.summary:
CISA has warned that SafePay ransomware actors have compromised at least 600 organizations across multiple critical infrastructure sectors, combining data theft and encryption with deliberate attacks on backup systems to obstruct recovery. The October 20, 2026, joint advisory describes operations spanning North America, South America, Europe, and Australia since August 2024. Published with the FBI, […]

articles.title: Rust 1.100 Will Let Developers Block Fresh Cargo Packages to Reduce Malware Supply Chain Risks
articles.summary:
Rust 1.100, scheduled for November 12, 2026, will introduce stable support for Cargo dependency cooldowns, allowing developers to reject newly published package versions until they reach a configurable minimum age. The feature gives security researchers, maintainers, and registries time to identify malicious releases before automated updates spread them across development environments and CI pipelines access. articles.title: Microsoft Introduces New Bug Bounty Rules That Could Affect Security Researchers’ Rewards
articles.summary:
Microsoft has introduced new rules for assessing reports in its bug bounty programs, tying submission completeness more directly to potential rewards. Announced by the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) on October 20, 2026, these changes replace the previous multiple report quality levels with two assessments: “Complete” and “Not Complete.” This updated approach establishes clearer expectations […]

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Compromised UpdraftCentral Keys to Install Malicious Plugins on WordPress Sites
articles.summary:
Attackers exploited compromised UpdraftCentral connection keys to send trusted remote-management commands to WordPress sites, ultimately installing malicious plugins that could provide unauthorized access to these websites. This incident followed unauthorized access to TeamUpdraft’s website on October 17-18, 2026. The company suspects attackers accessed its customer database, which contained UpdraftCentral connection keys and customer account information. […]

The post Hackers Exploit Compromised UpdraftCentral Keys to Install Malicious Plugins on WordPress Sites appeared first on GBHackers Security | #1 Globally Trusted Cyber Security News Platform.
